texts.preamble: Chethan Kumar S.R vs Nizam Bechan Khan on 1 December, 2025 Kabc020118582023 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.2629/2023 Dated this 1st day of December, 2025 Petitioner: Chethan Kumar S. R. Nizam Bechan Khan, Flat No.405, Khairane Village, Koparkhairne, Navimumbai, Maharashtra - 400 709. (Rc owner of Lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913) (Ex-parte) 2 Mvc No.2629/2023 2. (Policy No.VGC0888574000100, valid from 10-01-2023 to 09-01-2024) (Sri H. G. Srinivas, Advocate) Judgment
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 11-03-2023 at about 00.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-HF-626 towards Akkinalu Village, on the extreme left side of Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations. When he reached near Reliance Petrol Bunk, Binnamangala, Nelamangala, Bengaluru District, the driver of lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913, had parked the said lorry on two- wheeler passing road, without switching on the indicator or taking safety measures, in the early morning. Due to which the accident has occurred and the petitioner has fell down along with the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Manasvi Hospital, wherein he took conservative treatment and then he was shifted to Truelife Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient. Earlier to the accident, he was working in Blue Dart Courier and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said lorry, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing No.MH-43-Y-2913, vide policy bearing No.VGC0888574000100 in favour of respondent No.1 and it was valid from 10-01-2023 to 09-01-2024. Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the insured vehicle as on the date of accident. The Chethan Kumar S.R vs Nizam Bechan Khan on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141470471/ 2 owner of the vehicle knowing fully entrusted to drive the vehicle, who does not possess valid and effective driving licence. Thereby the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy. Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, no accident as stated in the claim petition has taken place, the lorry bearing Reg. No.MH- 43-Y-2913 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the petitioner has not sustained any injuries in the alleged accident, as stated in the claim petition. There is no nexus between injuries sustained to the petitioner and alleged accident. The alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner himself. The petitioner has filed a false petition to get unlawful gain. Further, it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. Further it is contended that, the lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913 was not possessing valid fitness certificate and permit to ply the said vehicle on the road. As such, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and rules and regulations of Motor Vehicles Act. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has not taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 29 years is 17. The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.16,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
